newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Unihold hits new year high on buy news.
newsitem.headline: Unihold hits new year high on buy news.

text.p: Shares in South African engineering firm Unihold Ltd soared on Tuesday after the company announced that it had bought Protea Technology Ltd (PTL), a reseller and manufacturer of high technology equipment.

By 0749 GMT Unihold stock had hit a new year high adding 65 cents or nearly 13 percent to 570 cents, making it the biggest early percentage gainer on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange. Some 165,700 shares worth around 883,125 rand had changed hands.

"I think they've gone up mainly on the back of the announcement they had this morning," one dealer said, adding that market players perceived the Unihold move to be positive for growth and profitability.
Unihold acquired PTL from Tradmin Engineering Holdings Ltd (TEHL), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Murray and Roberts Holdings Ltd.
The firm said earlier on Tuesday the acquisition was with effect from June 30, 1997.

It added that TEHL had agreed that the purchase price will not be less than 34.4 million rand and will be settled by the allotment of 8.05 million new Unihold shares which will be placed on behalf of TEHL with selected investors.

However, the acquisition was subject to the conclusion of a due diligence investigation by PTL, approval by TEHL and Unihold boards, the Johannesburg Stock Exchange granting a listing to the consideration shares and PTL's major principals sanctioning the change of control in PTL.
Unihold said the rationale behind the buy was that Murray and Roberts had embarked upon a controlled disposal strategy of non-core business and PTL was one of these.
"Unihold believes that the future growth prospects for PTL are most encouraging," it said.
